summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with Zsh as the shell, installs Oh-My-Zsh for a better command-line experience, and pre-populates a demo Git repository with some files and folder structure so users have something realistic to experiment with when the container starts.

explanations.3: This tells the installer to skip interactive prompts by setting a non-interactive mode, so the container build doesn't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag tells apt to skip optional packages that aren't strictly required, keeping the image smaller.
explanations.11: After installing packages, this removes apt's cache files to reduce the final image size since we don't need them anymore.
explanations.15: This downloads and runs Oh-My-Zsh's installation script directly from the internet using curl with flags for silent operation and error handling.
explanations.16: The empty string and flags here pass arguments to the installation script: the empty string is a placeholder, and --unattended --keep-zshrc tell it to install without prompts and keep the default config file.
explanations.21: This sets up Git's global configuration so any commits made in the container have an author identity.
explanations.25: The -q flag makes git init quiet (no output), and -b main sets the default branch name to 'main' instead of 'master'.
explanations.31: This sets the default directory where the shell will start, placing you deep in the nested folder structure for testing cd navigation features.
explanations.37: The -i flag makes the shell interactive, and -l makes it a login shell, so it reads startup files and feels like a real terminal session.
